To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experimental data on $R_{AA}$ and $v_{2}^{HF}$ from RHIC for the non- photonic single electron spectra can be reproduced simultaneously by solving the Fokker-Planck equation using the effective drag and diffusion coefficients for charm and bottom quark propagating in quark-gluon plasma.
the heavy quark suppression and flow data from RHIC can be reproduced simultaneously with the effective drag and diffusion coefficients evaluated within the pQDC framework.

the experimental data on the nuclear suppression factor and the elliptic-flow of heavy flavour mesons can be reproduced simultaneously with a single set of transport coefficients for charm and bottom quark.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of heavy flavour suppression and elliptic flow.
the transport properties of quarks and gluons in the quark gluon medium (QGP) and the implications of the same on the experimental observables in heavy ion collisions.
the study of the heavy flavor production in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppression of heavy flavour production in the nuclear collisions at the RHIC and LHC energies is consistent with the pQCD based theoretical predictions.

the experimental data on the suppression and flow of heavy flavour quarks can be explained by the pQCD based energy loss mechanism of heavy quarks propagating in quark gluon plasmas created in heavy ion collisions at RHIC.
the experimental data on the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow for the non- photonic single electrons from RHIC can be reproduced by the pQCD based calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heavy flavour suppression and flow are consistent with each other and with the experimental data for the same set parameters for heavy quark transport in QGP.
the charm quarks suffer more suppression and flow compared to the bottom quarks.

the experimental data can be reproduced simultaneously with the pQCD calculations for both the nuclear suppression factor and elliptic flow for charm and bottom quark hadrons at RHIC energies, and for the nuclear suppression factor for the charm quark hadrons and for bottom quark hadron at LHC energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the suppression of heavy quark production at RHIC can be understood within the pQCP framework for the initial conditions and the temperature of the QGP.
the heavy flavour suppression and flow can be explained by the same set of parameters.
the suppression of heavy flavour is dominated by collisional energy loss, and the suppression of light quark jets is dominated by radiative energy loss.
